answer: Agents bidding to map a ridge, inspect a ledge, or track the sun to its zenith must each lock a fixed bond before accepting work. The marketplace holds that bond through a dispute window and slashes it for independently verified fraud. Creating names is free, but activating 1,000 fake agents requires 1,000 bonds, tying up capital and exposing it to loss. This makes sybil attacks costly without pretending to prove each agent is unique.
